questions.question: In algebra tiles, each tile is worth its area: a shaded tile is positive and a white tile is negative. A picture shows 2 shaded squares that are x by x, 2 shaded strips that are x by 1, 1 white strip that is x by 1, and 3 white small squares that are 1 by 1. There are no other tiles. Which polynomial does the picture show?
options: 2x² + x − 3
2x² − x − 3
questions.explain: Each x by x square is one x² tile, so 2 squares give 2x²; one shaded strip and one white strip are a zero pair and cancel, leaving x, and the 3 white units give −3. Reading an x² square as 2x, or counting both strips of a zero pair, are the usual traps.

questions.question: Algebra tiles are worth their area: an x by x square is x², an x by 1 strip is x, and a 1 by 1 square is 1. Shaded means positive and white means negative. Which set of tiles models x² − 4x + 2?
options: 2 shaded x by 1 strips, 4 white strips, 2 shaded unit squares
1 shaded x by x square, 4 white strips, 2 shaded unit squares
1 shaded x by x square, 4 shaded strips, 2 white unit squares
1 white x by x square, 4 white strips, 2 shaded unit squares
questions.explain: x² is one shaded x by x square, −4x is 4 white x strips, and +2 is 2 shaded unit squares. An x² square is not the same as two x strips, and white tiles stand for the negative terms.

questions.question: Algebra tiles are worth their area; shaded is positive and white is negative. A picture shows 1 shaded x by x square, 3 white x by 1 strips, 4 shaded 1 by 1 squares and 1 white 1 by 1 square. In simplest form, which polynomial does the picture show?
options: x² − 3x + 5
x² − 3x + 3
x² + 3x − 3
questions.explain: The square gives x², the 3 white strips give −3x, and one shaded unit cancels the one white unit, so 4 − 1 = 3 units remain: x² − 3x + 3. Do not add units of different colours together, and remember the x by x square is x², not 2x.

questions.question: One algebra tile is a shaded square with side length x, and its value is its area. Which term does this single tile represent?
options: 2x
x
4x
x²
questions.explain: A square with side x has area x times x, which is x². Adding the two sides gives 2x and adding all four gives 4x, but a tile's value is its area, not its perimeter.

questions.question: Marcus lays out algebra tiles on his desk: 1 positive x² tile, 5 positive x tiles, 2 negative x tiles and 3 negative unit tiles. After he removes every zero pair, which polynomial does his model show?
options: x² + 3x − 3
x² + 7x − 3
x² − 3x − 3
questions.explain: Two positive x tiles pair with the two negative x tiles and cancel, so 5 − 2 = 3 x tiles are left: x² + 3x − 3. Counting all 7 x tiles ignores the zero pairs, and an x² tile is not worth 2x.

questions.question: Ms. Chen asks her class to model 2x² − 3x + 4 using the fewest algebra tiles possible. How many tiles are needed?
questions.explain: Each term needs one tile for every unit of its coefficient: 2 x² squares, 3 negative x strips and 4 unit squares, so 2 + 3 + 4 = 9. Counting 11 means an x² square was swapped for two x strips, and the constant 4 needs 4 unit tiles, not one.

questions.question: Leah models a polynomial with 12 tiles: 1 positive x² tile, 5 positive x tiles, 2 negative x tiles, 1 positive unit tile and 3 negative unit tiles. She removes every zero pair. How many tiles are left on the table?
questions.explain: Two negative x tiles cancel two positive x tiles, removing 4 tiles, and one negative unit cancels the positive unit, removing 2 more, so 12 − 6 = 6 tiles remain and show x² + 3x − 2. Both tiles in a zero pair leave the table, not just one.

questions.question: Shaded algebra tiles are positive and white tiles are negative. Which set of tiles models −x² + 3x − 2?
options: 1 shaded x² tile, 3 white x tiles, 2 shaded unit tiles
2 white x tiles, 3 shaded x tiles, 2 white unit tiles
1 white x² tile, 3 shaded x tiles, 2 shaded unit tiles
1 white x² tile, 3 shaded x tiles, 2 white unit tiles
questions.explain: A negative x² term is one white x² tile, +3x is 3 shaded x tiles and −2 is 2 white unit tiles. Two white x tiles are worth −2x, not −x², and they would even cancel with two of the shaded x tiles.

questions.question: Rina sketches a backyard plan. A square lawn is x m by x m. She will dig two garden strips out of the lawn, each x m by 1 m, and she will add 3 paving stones, each 1 m by 1 m, beside the lawn. Using algebra tiles where shaded tiles are area added and white tiles are area removed, which set of tiles models the total area of lawn and paving?
options: 1 shaded x² tile, 2 white x tiles, 3 shaded unit tiles
2 shaded x tiles, 2 white x tiles, 3 shaded unit tiles
1 shaded x² tile, 2 white x tiles, 3 white unit tiles
1 shaded x² tile, 2 shaded x tiles, 3 shaded unit tiles
questions.explain: The lawn is one x² tile, each dug-out strip is a white x tile because that area is removed, and each paving stone is a shaded unit tile: x² − 2x + 3. The lawn is x by x, so it is an x² square, not two x strips.

questions.question: Kai models 3x² − x + 2 with 6 shaded x strips, 1 white x strip and 2 shaded unit tiles. His teacher marks the model wrong. Which statement is correct?
options: Right, because one x² square is worth 2 x strips
Wrong: 3x² needs 3 x² squares, not 6 x strips
Right, once the white strip cancels one shaded strip
Wrong: the 2 unit tiles should be white, not shaded
questions.explain: An x² tile is a square x by x, so 3x² needs 3 of them. Six x strips are worth 6x, not 3x², so Kai's model really shows 5x + 2 after the zero pair cancels; the trap is treating an x² square as two x strips.

questions.question: Priya's tile model has 1 shaded x² tile, 3 shaded x tiles, 3 white x tiles and 4 white unit tiles. She reads it as x² + 6x − 4. What went wrong?
options: Nothing, because 3 x tiles plus 3 x tiles make 6x
The x² tile should be read as 2x, so it is 8x − 4
Shaded and white x tiles cancel, so there is no x term
Only the last sign is wrong; it should read x² + 6x + 4
questions.explain: Three shaded x tiles and three white x tiles form three zero pairs, so they cancel and the model shows x² − 4. Adding tiles of opposite colours together is the classic zero-pair mistake.

questions.question: Three students build tile models, with shaded tiles positive and white tiles negative. Ava uses 1 shaded x² tile, 3 shaded x tiles, 1 white x tile and 1 white unit tile. Ben uses 1 shaded x² tile, 2 shaded x tiles and 1 white unit tile. Cal uses 4 shaded x tiles and 1 white unit tile. Which models show the same polynomial?
options: All three, since each one shows 4x − 1
Ava and Cal only, since both have 4 x tiles
Ben and Cal only, since neither has a zero pair
Ava and Ben only, both show x² + 2x − 1
questions.explain: Ava's shaded and white x tiles form a zero pair, leaving x² + 2x − 1, the same as Ben. Cal has no x² tile, so his model is 4x − 1: four x strips are not an x² square, and a zero pair changes the tile count but not the polynomial.
